<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(iv) Directors&#8217; Compensation Plan (&#8220;Directors&#8217; Plan&#8221;)</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non-management directors of the Company receive a minimum of 50%, and may elect to receive a greater portion, of their fees in common stock.&#160;&#160;The number of shares of common stock to be issued to non-management directors is determined by dividing the dollar value of the fees by the closing price of the common stock on the relevant payment date.&#160;&#160;The maximum number of shares of common stock available to be issued by the Company under the Directors&#8217; Plan is 5,000,000.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the year ended December 31, 2016, the Company issued 268,239<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>shares of<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>common stock with a fair value of $210 as payment of fees and retainers due to non-management directors.&#160;&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2015, the Company issued 290,575<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>shares of<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>common stock with a fair value of $198 as payment of fees and retainers due to non-management directors.&#160;&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2014, the Company issued 156,226 shares of common stock with a fair value of $179<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>as payment of fees and retainers due to non-management directors.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">12. Promissory Notes Receivable</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 17, 2008, prior to its merger with NeuLion, Inc., NeuLion USA, Inc. loaned employees an aggregate of $209 through promissory notes to exercise stock options.&#160; The promissory notes bear interest at 3.16% per annum and were repayable on October 17, 2013.&#160; The Company extended the repayment of the promissory notes from October 17, 2013 to October 17, 2017.&#160; During the year ended December 31, 2016, an employee repaid $20 plus interest.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">13. Earnings Per Share</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing net income for the year by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding for the period.&#160; Diluted earnings per share is computed by dividing net income for the year by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding adjusted for the dilutive effect of preferred stock, restricted stock units, stock options and warrants.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As at December 31, 2016, the Company had federal and state net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $63,119 and $39,828, respectively.&#160; The federal and state net operating losses do not include approximately $20,056 and $14,867, respectively, related to tax goodwill amortization that will not be realized for financial reporting purposes until the Company is able to take a tax benefit for those deductions. The federal and state net operating losses begin to expire in 2024 and 2017, respectively.&#160; As at December 31, 2016, the Company had federal and state research and development credit carryforwards of approximately $210 and $86, respectively.&#160; The federal research and development credit begins to expire in 2033. The state research and development credit carries forward indefinitely. As at December 31, 2016, the Company had a foreign tax credit carryforward of approximately $10,834.&#160; The Company had foreign net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $11,826. Our ability to utilize our federal tax attribute carryforwards have been limited by Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;), which imposes an annual limit on the ability of a corporation that undergoes an ''ownership change'' to use its tax attribute carryforwards to reduce its liability.&#160; An ownership change is generally defined as a greater than 50% increase in equity ownership by 5% shareholders in any three-year period.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As at December 31, 2015, based on the weight of available evidence, including profitability in recent periods and the availability of expected future taxable income, the Company concluded that it is more likely than not that the benefits of federal and some state-related deferred income tax assets will be realized. Accordingly, the Company reduced the valuation allowances on its federal gross deferred income tax assets. The Company continues to maintain a valuation allowance to offset foreign and certain state deferred tax assets, as realization of such assets do not meet the more-likely-than-not threshold. The net change in the total valuation allowance was a decrease of $(504) and an increase of $39,105 for the year ended December 31, 2016 and December 31, 2015, respectively.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company accounts for income taxes in accordance with ASC Topic 740, &#8220;Income Taxes Recognition.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The Company does not believe there are any material uncertain tax provisions under ASC 740.&#160;&#160;The Company is subject to federal and state income tax, as well as income tax in various foreign jurisdictions in which the Company operates. The Company&#8217;s federal and state tax returns remain open and subject to potential government audit for the years 2013, 2014 and 2015. However, to the extent allowed by law the tax authorities may have the right to examine prior periods where net operating losses or tax credits were generated and carried forward, and make adjustments up to the amount of the net operating losses or credit carryforward amount.</div>
